values.note: Electric sites $25 a night in season, $5 less mid-October through April; the four primitive sites ($10) are closed by flood damage. Pay by envelope at the self-service box. Plus tax and a park entry permit ($7 a day for a Nebraska vehicle, $14 otherwise; $35 / $70 a year).

note: NGPC recreation area on a Logan Creek/Elkhorn oxbow off US 275, ~4 mi north of Scribner, beside Powder Horn WMA. 17 electric sites (30 A) in a loop at the south end of the oxbow; the four primitive sites have been closed by flood damage. First-come first-served, self-pay envelopes. Drinking water, primitive restrooms; no dump station. --Claude
summary: Grid row 'E P' confirmed; 17 x 30 A electric, primitive sites closed by flood damage (NGPC page snippet). Base fee moved from the closed $10 primitive to electric $20-25. Pin is ~650 m off, in a farm field east of the county road -> move to the campground loop. Not waterfront kept (treed bank, loop road). Phone 402-727-2922 missing.
flags: PIN MOVE: stored 41.7172,-96.6818 is in a crop field east of the county road, ~650 m from the park. The campground loop (two-branch gravel loop with pads, ~100 m across, at the south end of the oxbow off the park road) is at ~41.7139,-96.6884. The other developed spots are a small turnaround with a shelter in the oxbow's middle (~41.7173,-96.6873, ramp/day use) and a maintenance building at the north entrance. NGPC's page (blocked) has no map I could read, so the loop is identified from imagery only.

FEES: base was $10 primitive, but those four sites are closed ('due to flood damage, the four Primitive campsites are not available at this time' - NGPC page, snippet, undated); base now electric $25 in season / $20 off-season per the 2025 grid. The closure is undated; if the primitive sites reopen, $10 primitive is the base again.
PHONE missing: 402-727-2922 (NGPC 2025 camping rates grid, Dead Timber row). Website https://outdoornebraska.gov/location/dead-timber/ is the right page (blocked, unread directly).

WATERFRONT not waterfront kept: the loop's north arc is ~20-40 m from the oxbow with a wooded bank between and the loop road inside; no site shows open ground to the water, and imagery under canopy cannot confirm. The oxbow is narrow (~30-40 m) and duckweed-covered.
STATUS: the four primitive sites closed (partial, undated); the electric loop operates. Not written as a closure.
